concepts.why: The answer gives no rule about print or println. Its error comes from how the loop runs, not from printing.
The answer says nothing about how the loop variable is set, tested and updated. Its wrong claim is about when a while loop exits, so it is graded under while_loop.

concepts.way: misconception: The loop stops the moment the condition becomes false, even in the middle of the body.
concepts.quote: When n becomes 4 the loop stops before the print.
concepts.why: Java only checks the condition before each pass, so the pass that sets n to 4 still prints 4 and the output is "2 4 ", not "2".
The answer never states a fact that holds on every pass, or a reason the loop ends.
